```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Massive migrations of exploited workers, refugees, displaced farmers, agricultural workers, and asylum seekers result from an unjust global political and economic system that benefits transnational corporations and harms the world’s peoples.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Immigration to the United States results from both the pull of greater economic opportunity and the push of growing economic inequality and exploitation in developing societies.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Much of the current wave of migration to the United States from Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean can be traced to NAFTA and other unjust free trade agreements.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"NAFTA and other unjust free trade agreements enabled subsidized U.S. agribusiness to flood Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean with cheap produce, destroying the livelihoods of millions of small farmers and other rural workers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The export-oriented, often capital-intensive form of manufacturing imposed by the IMF, World Bank, and WTO limits the number of good jobs in the urban economy of developing nations.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The same story about migration can be told about African migration to the nations of the European Union.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The push for mass immigration from the developing world can be stemmed if these economies are allowed to develop in equitable and internally integrated ways.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Equitable and internally integrated development would require the national and international regulation of corporate power by free trade unions and democratic governments.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Equitable and internally integrated development would require the democratization of international economic regulatory institutions.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
